excerpt: No more re-entering IPs, ports, or password. Everything is saved, so you connect instantly.
if you configure a jump host for a Group, every Host within it will automatically connect through that jump host
Items in the Keychain can be referenced by multiple Hosts and Groups without duplicating them.
You can broadcast a command to all sessions simultaneously and save the entire setup as a reusable template.
execute them on multiple hosts at once from the Snippets screen
Termius can convert a plain-language description into a shell command... Termius generates the command using AI.
Termius automatically collects terminal session logs for every host. Logs are synced across devices and shared with your team. You can search logs and save them using Bookmarks.
Every account includes a Personal vault, accessible only to you and synced across all your devices.
When you add team members, a Team vault is created automatically. This vault is shared with all team members, allowing your team to manage infrastructure together.
Collaborate in the terminal in real-time using the multiplayer sessions. Troubleshoot together or guide teammates through your workflow.
With autocomplete suggestions for frequently used commands, arguments, and file paths, you can save time and focus on more important things.
Create and manage your SSH keys with passphrase protection. Everything is encrypted and easily accessible from any device.
Secure SSH authentication with FIDO2 security keys and MFA.
Secure connections with device-bound keys and biometric protection with Windows Hello, Touch ID/Face ID, or Android biometrics.
Termius doesn't depend on the cloud to manage your access. Your infrastructure is stored and encrypted locally. Connect directly to your servers without the internet, a proxy, or VPN.

Combination of Termius's saved snippets and short shell scripts let me do monitoring without running a separate web-server behind auth. Easier to build an interactive shell script than an interactive webpage.
Saved my butt once when my docker containers were bouncing while on vacation—debugged and deployed a fix from my iPhone while my wife drove. Supporting Mosh for free is a huge plus.

Termius on Windows falls short of usability threshold due to slow performance at high resolutions—scrolling large text is much worse than gnome-terminal or Terminal.app. Issue persists after reinstalling every few months.
I'm usually wary of using closed-source programs for sensitive tasks like SSH. I haven't found details on the crypto libraries used or security steps taken.
Great app but the ability to remap caps lock to Esc on an external iPad keyboard is why I went with Blink shell instead.
I'm a hobbyist, so the subscription isn't justified for me (plus I don't like subscriptions). Wish there was a one-time-purchase App Store option instead.
New development in the past six months no longer supports older iPhone/iPad models where I had Termius installed.
Not sure if I missed something, but I can't add custom fonts.
187MB for an installer! What extra do we get instead of Putty/other SSH clients to justify this humongous size? Can't the size be slimmed down?
I cannot scroll with the mouse and select text in the Mac app, so I still have to use Mac Terminal for log collection. Also skeptical about storing hostnames/IPs/passwords on a third-party app.
Product and website claim over 24,000 engineers in one section and 300,000 in another, and 10,000 on the pricing page—it's confusing and makes me question credibility.
Wow, this app saved my butt over a year ago when I ran out of laptop battery in the field.
I love using Termius on my 12.9” iPad Pro with keyboard—full screen terminal with extra features that pop up right when needed.
Termius on Windows is slow and buggy; little has been done to address this for at least the past two years.

It's yet another subscription, cheapest $8.33/month, more than Microsoft Office. Enterprise at $29/month is unreasonable—as an org of 1,000 engineers we're not using it. Prefer VanDyke's SecureCRT/FX with responsive support.
The only benefit of Termius seems to be a few nice colours, with the downside of being able to store your SSH keys on Termius' servers.
I have no idea what Termius is, but your landing page takes over 4 seconds to show anything on Firefox even on a repeat visit.
I haven't tried the Terminal Sharing feature yet but I have found Termius to be one of the best SSH clients on iOS and iPadOS.
With tmate, only one person needs the tool—the other can SSH in or view it in a browser. Termius requires both sides to have Termius for sharing to work.
